title.rendered: Blessed Is the One: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Blessed is the one whose delight is in the law of the Lord, who meditates on it day and night. They are like a tree planted by streams of water. Their leaves do not wither.

content.rendered:
Blessed is the one whose delight is in the law of the Lord, who meditates on it day and night. They are like a tree planted by streams of water. Their leaves do not wither. Whatever they do prospers.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, June 21, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed is the one who does not walk in step with the wicked or stand in the way that sinners take or sit in the company of mockers, but whose delight is in the law of the Lord, and who meditates on his law day and night. That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither—whatever they do prospers.”
Psalm 1:1-3 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Psalm 1 sits at the threshold of the entire Psalter. Whoever arranged the Psalms placed this one first as the gatekeeper. Before you enter the songs of David, the laments of Asaph, the praise of the sons of Korah, you must walk through Psalm 1. It tells you the secret of the blessed life. And the secret has very little to do with circumstances. It has almost everything to do with where the mind dwells.

The psalmist describes the blessed person in two ways. First by what they refuse. They do not walk in step with the wicked. They do not stand in the way of sinners. They do not sit in the company of mockers. Notice the progression. Walking. Standing. Sitting. Each verb is more settled than the last. The blessed person refuses the slow slide from passing influence to permanent residence. They do not let bad company become their home.

Second, the blessed person is described by what they love. Their delight is in the law of the Lord. They meditate on it day and night. The Hebrew word for meditate, hagah, is the same word used for the low rumbling sound a lion makes over its prey. It is a deep, satisfied dwelling. The blessed person does not flick through Scripture once a week and move on. They chew on it. They rumble over it. They return to it morning and evening. The Word lives in them as a presence, not a duty.

And the result is the picture every dry soul longs for. A tree planted by streams of water. Roots deep. Fruit in season. Leaves that do not wither. Whatever they do prospers. This is not a magic prosperity formula. This is the natural fruit of a life rooted in living water. The roots reach the source. The source supplies the tree. The tree, in its season, yields what God designed it to yield. The drought outside does not destroy what the underground source is keeping alive.

For Sunday, this is the picture worth carrying into worship. The believer is not a tumbleweed at the mercy of every wind that blows. The believer is a tree, planted by the streams of God’s word, rooted by the Spirit, drawing on a source the surface world cannot see. The drought may come. The leaves do not wither. The fruit comes in its season.

So delight in His word today. Meditate on it. Let it rumble in you. Tomorrow’s strength is being drawn from the roots you sink today.

Prayer

Father, plant me by Your streams of water. Sink my roots deep into Your word. Make me a person whose delight is in Your law and whose meditation runs through every hour. Let me yield fruit in season. Let my leaf not wither. And in every drought of life, let the world see that the source of my life is hidden in You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am blessed. My delight is in the law of the Lord. I meditate on His word day and night. I am like a tree planted by streams of water. My leaf does not wither. My fruit comes in season. Whatever the Lord leads me to do, He prospers.
